name: Tutorial Jr. Sentinel
description: A training dummy found in the Tutorial area of Maple Island. Tutorial Jr. Sentinel is completely harmless and serves as target practice for brand new adventurers learning the basics of combat.

movement.label: Stays on its floor
movement.description: Walks back and forth on the floor it spawns on.

gaps: mesos per kill: no player reports on MeowDB (see drops/1.json)
drop chances and quantities: MeowDB gives none (see drops/1.json)
kb (knockback threshold), boss/undead tags, hp/mp recovery and revive data are not shown on the detail page; taken from MeowDB's simulator data chunk (field_sources)
attacks: the page lists no attack entries (skills, ranged or magic attacks) for this monster, only the touch zone; touch-damage rules live in the formulas domain (/formulas/damage-taken)

monster knockback: MeowDB publishes only the KB threshold (knockback_threshold_damage). How far, how high or how long a monster is pushed or staggered when hit is not published; the "Knockback Airtime" model on https://meowdb.com/msclassic/formulas/damage-taken sits under "After You Get Hit" and describes the PLAYER being knocked back, not monsters

Peace vs touch damage: this page marks the monster "Peace" ("Non-aggressive, won't attack unless provoked") and its analysis says "Non-aggressive (PEACE), won't attack unless you hit it first. Safe to walk past.", yet the same page shows a 21 x 36 px touch zone, Touch DMG 1-1 (Base 1) and the generic Combat Details text "The touch zone deals contact damage when you walk into it. Attack power is a percent of the monster's own damage stat: physical attacks use P.DMG, magic attacks use M.DMG.". MeowDB does not say whether walking into a Peace monster's touch zone damages the player

values.value: Multiplier on how many monsters that map keeps alive at once, on top of its spawn-point count. Above 1.0 means a fuller map. Not applied to the respawn figures yet.
values.source: https://meowdb.com/msclassic/monsters/1 (Map Locations "Mob Rate" column tooltip; i18n string in https://meowdb.com/_next/static/chunks/app/msclassic/%5Blocale%5D/monsters/%5Bid%5D/page-69d6e8d28a1ff596.js)

values.value: About mob rate. Mob rate multiplies how many monsters this map keeps alive at once. This map has 6 spawn points and a mob rate of 0.6x, so expect about 4 monsters up at a time instead of 6. The spawn figures above do not apply it yet. This is our best reading from closed-beta play, where a high-rate map held far more monsters than it has spawn points; an exact whole-map count has not been done.

How many mobs a map keeps alive at once. Set by the map's spawn-point count scaled by party size (about 75% of the points filled solo, rising to 100% in a full six-player party). There is no separate map-wide multiplier or fixed 40-mob cap.

discrepancies.chosen: mob_rate is kept verbatim as MeowDB publishes it; the extractor applies no multiplier and derives no capacity
discrepancies.reason: MeowDB disagrees with itself: the monster-page tooltip and the map pages call mob rate a multiplier on how many monsters a map keeps alive (the map page calls it "our best reading from closed-beta play" and does not apply it to its own figures), while the glossary says live capacity is the spawn-point count scaled by party size with no separate map-wide multiplier; the https://meowdb.com/msclassic/formulas/spawns capacity model ("Capacity = floor(SpawnPoints × PlayerScalar)") has no mob-rate term. Whether the game applies mob_rate is a MisoStory design decision, not canonical data

notes: MeowDB (Touch DMG tooltip): Estimated touch damage at 0 WDEF. Base P.DMG: 1. Use the calculator for your level and total WDEF.

MeowDB (touch zone tooltip): The dashed rectangle is the touch damage zone: players touching it take the P.DMG contact damage. Width x height from the game frame data; drawn anchored to the bottom center of the sprite.
MeowDB (Combat Details): The touch zone deals contact damage when you walk into it. Attack power is a percent of the monster's own damage stat: physical attacks use P.DMG, magic attacks use M.DMG.
MeowDB (animation): Die: body fades over 780ms; loot drops as soon as the mob dies.
MeowDB analysis: Non-aggressive (PEACE), won't attack unless you hit it first. Safe to walk past.

Respawn: "wave" spawn points respawn on MeowDB's modelled global 7.56 s server tick plus a 5 s per-point cooldown (the page shows "~7.5s"); "timed" points use respawn_min_s..respawn_max_s. See https://meowdb.com/msclassic/formulas/spawns (retrieved 2026-10-04T10:04:46.189Z).
